Looking at this problem, I need to solve the wave equation in the upper half-space with Dirichlet boundary conditions using the method of images.

**Interpretation of the PDE:** The equation $\Delta u = u_{tt} = 0$ is the homogeneous wave equation $u_{tt} - \Delta u = 0$ (wave speed $c=1$) in $\Omega = \{x_3 > 0\} \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, with initial data $\Phi, \Psi$ and Dirichlet boundary condition $u = 0$ on $\{x_3 = 0\}$.

---

## Setup: Method of Images (Odd Reflection)

Since the boundary condition is $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega = \{x_3 = 0\}$, we use **odd reflection** across the boundary. Define the reflected point $x^* = (x_1, x_2, -x_3)$, and extend the initial data to all of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by odd symmetry in $x_3$:

$$\tilde{\Phi}(x) = \begin{cases} \Phi(x) & x_3 > 0, \\ -\Phi(x^*) & x_3 < 0, \end{cases} \qquad \tilde{\Psi}(x) = \begin{cases} \Psi(x) & x_3 > 0, \\ -\Psi(x^*) & x_3 < 0. \end{cases}$$

(We assume the compatibility conditions $\Phi\big|_{x_3=0} = \Psi\big|_{x_3=0} = 0$ so that $\tilde\Phi, \tilde\Psi$ are sufficiently smooth.)

The free-space Kirchhoff formula in $\mathbb{R}^3$ applied to $\tilde\Phi, \tilde\Psi$ gives:

$$u(x,t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\!\left[\frac{1}{4\pi t}\int_{|y-x|=t} \tilde\Phi(y)\,dS_y\right] + \frac{1}{4\pi t}\int_{|y-x|=t} \tilde\Psi(y)\,dS_y. \tag{$\star$}$$

Since $\tilde\Phi, \tilde\Psi$ are odd in $x_3$, the solution $u$ is odd in $x_3$, hence $u\big|_{x_3=0} = 0$, satisfying the boundary condition. Restricted to $\Omega$, this solves our IBVP.

---

## Part (a): Formula for $t < x_3$

When $t < x_3$, every point $y$ on the sphere $|y - x| = t$ satisfies

$$y_3 \geq x_3 - t > 0,$$

so the entire sphere lies in the upper half-space. Therefore $\tilde\Phi(y) = \Phi(y)$ and $\tilde\Psi(y) = \Psi(y)$ on the whole sphere, and $(\star)$ reduces to the **free-space Kirchhoff formula**:

$$\boxed{u(x,t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\!\left[\frac{1}{4\pi t}\int_{|y-x|=t} \Phi(y)\,dS_y\right] + \frac{1}{4\pi t}\int_{|y-x|=t} \Psi(y)\,dS_y, \qquad t < x_3.}$$

Equivalently, via the parametrization $y = x + ts$, $|s| = 1$:

$$u(x,t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\!\left[\frac{t}{4\pi}\int_{|s|=1} \Phi(x+ts)\,dS_s\right] + \frac{t}{4\pi}\int_{|s|=1} \Psi(x+ts)\,dS_s.$$

**Physical interpretation:** The wave has not yet reached the boundary, so the boundary condition has no effect — the solution coincides with the free-space solution.

---

## Part (b): Formula for all $t > 0$

When $t \geq x_3$, the sphere $|y - x| = t$ crosses the plane $y_3 = 0$ and extends into $y_3 < 0$, where $\tilde\Phi$ and $\tilde\Psi$ take reflected (negated) values. We split the sphere into the upper part $\{y_3 > 0\}$ and lower part $\{y_3 < 0\}$.

**Upper part** ($y_3 > 0$): $\tilde\Phi(y) = \Phi(y)$, $\tilde\Psi(y) = \Psi(y)$.

**Lower part** ($y_3 < 0$): $\tilde\Phi(y) = -\Phi(y_1, y_2, -y_3)$, $\tilde\Psi(y) = -\Psi(y_1, y_2, -y_3)$.

In the lower-part integrals, substitute $z = (y_1, y_2, -y_3)$ (so $z_3 > 0$). Since reflection preserves surface measure ($dS_y = dS_z$), and

$$|z - x^*|^2 = (y_1 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - x_2)^2 + (-y_3 + x_3)^2 = |y - x|^2 = t^2,$$

the lower-part integral transforms into an integral over the portion of the **reflected sphere** $|z - x^*| = t$ lying in $z_3 > 0$.

Define the **partial spherical mean**:

$$\mathcal{M}_f(\xi, t) := \frac{1}{4\pi t}\int_{\substack{|y - \xi| = t \\ y_3 > 0}} f(y)\,dS_y.$$

Then $(\star)$ becomes:

$$\boxed{u(x,t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\Big[\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x,t) - \mathcal{M}_\Phi(x^*,t)\Big] + \Big[\mathcal{M}_\Psi(x,t) - \mathcal{M}_\Psi(x^*,t)\Big], \qquad t > 0,\; x \in \Omega,}$$

where $x^* = (x_1, x_2, -x_3)$. Written out explicitly:

$$u(x,t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\!\left\{\frac{1}{4\pi t}\!\left[\int_{\substack{|y-x|=t\\y_3>0}}\!\!\Phi(y)\,dS_y \;-\; \int_{\substack{|y-x^*|=t\\y_3>0}}\!\!\Phi(y)\,dS_y\right]\right\} + \frac{1}{4\pi t}\!\left[\int_{\substack{|y-x|=t\\y_3>0}}\!\!\Psi(y)\,dS_y \;-\; \int_{\substack{|y-x^*|=t\\y_3>0}}\!\!\Psi(y)\,dS_y\right].$$

---

## Verification

**Boundary condition ($x_3 = 0$):** When $x_3 = 0$, we have $x = x^*$, so $\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x,t) = \mathcal{M}_\Phi(x^*,t)$ and $\mathcal{M}_\Psi(x,t) = \mathcal{M}_\Psi(x^*,t)$. The two terms in each bracket cancel, giving $u = 0$. ✓

**Initial condition $u(x,0) = \Phi(x)$:** As $t \to 0^+$ with $x_3 > 0$, the sphere $|y - x| = t$ shrinks to $x \in \Omega$, so $\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x,t) \to \Phi(x)$. Meanwhile $x^*_3 = -x_3 < 0$, so for small $t$ the sphere $|y - x^*| = t$ lies entirely in $y_3 < 0$, giving $\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x^*,t) = 0$. The time-derivative term vanishes at $t = 0$ (standard property: $\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{M}_\Phi\big|_{t=0} = 0$ by symmetry of the sphere). Thus $u(x,0) = \Phi(x)$. ✓

**Initial condition $u_t(x,0) = \Psi(x)$:** Similarly, $\mathcal{M}_\Psi(x,t) \to \Psi(x)$ and $\mathcal{M}_\Psi(x^*,t) \to 0$ as $t \to 0^+$. The second time derivative of the spherical mean vanishes at $t=0$ by symmetry ($\int_{|s|=1} \nabla\Phi(x)\cdot s\,dS_s = 0$). Thus $u_t(x,0) = \Psi(x)$. ✓

**PDE:** The formula $(\star)$ is the Kirchhoff solution to the free-space wave equation with data $\tilde\Phi, \tilde\Psi$. Restricted to $\Omega$, it satisfies $\Delta u = u_{tt}$ in $\Omega$. ✓

**Consistency with part (a):** When $t < x_3$, the sphere $|y - x| = t$ lies entirely in $y_3 > 0$, so $\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x,t)$ is the full spherical mean. The reflected sphere $|y - x^*| = t$ has center at $x^*_3 = -x_3 < 0$ and radius $t < x_3$, so it lies entirely in $y_3 < 0$, giving $\mathcal{M}_\Phi(x^*,t) = 0$. The formula reduces to the free-space Kirchhoff formula of part (a). ✓
